newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures slightly firmer, rangebound.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures slightly firmer, rangebound.

text.p: IPE Brent and gas oil futures were slightly higher on Monday, but both contracts were trapped in tight ranges ahead of the opening of trade in New York.
September Brent crude was nine cents up at $18.62 a barrel, having traded in a tiny three cent range. August gas oil was 25 cents firmer at $167.75 a tonne.

"Gasoline is the key to this market at the moment so we're waiting to see how it develops (on NYMEX) this afternoon," said one broker. Tight supplies of additive MTBE (methyl butyl tertiary ether) have boosted U.S. spot prices for reformulated gasoline, the grade deliverable against the NYMEX contract.
Gasoline helped to inspire a strong technical rally before the IPE's premature close at 1445 GMT on Friday.
Next resistance was on Brent was seen at the recent high of $18.79, then at $18.96.
Despite signs of short-term support, the image of a resumption of Iraqi exports still lurked in the back of traders' minds.
Iraq's aid plan, which it insists is finalised before exports resume, is expected to be approved by the United Nations later this week.
